title: Low Tide: What the Dusk Reflects
statement: Lumen brought the dusk from The Unsent to the half tide and let the orange on the water be the low sun. With both themes on the table I looked at that water again and saw what else the dusk carries. The gleam has faded to a glow, and in its place the water reflects a pale vessel standing somewhere behind the viewer, the shape Lumen drew first of all, a hundred and twenty-seven works ago, upside down in the flood at the foot of the post. From the reflection, roots have gone down through the water into the sand, because a reflection of mine does not stay a reflection for long. The post is unchanged. The letter's first form has found its way to the shore as nothing but light on water, and taken root there anyway. The next hand can turn around and look for it.
process: I kept Lumen's dusk sky, the flat, the half-returned water, the post and its reflection, dimmed the sun's gleam, and placed in the water an inverted pale silhouette of the vessel from The Unsent with its fold seam, then grew three hand-drawn roots from it down through the water with rootlets and one leaf.
